# Legacy core audit: correctness work queue

Independent static review, 2026-10-20. Baseline:
`41bd7000363f34b1e7e2d7e354971bfe9021e2b1` (relevant implementation blobs also
match `5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb`). These are source findings,
not reproduced runtime failures unless a later entry supplies a regression test
and exact CI result. Do not infer that existing Rust behavior is a requirement.

## Highest risks

| Finding and baseline source | Required correction and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Overlapping docs/output/cache paths; docs `.` or ancestor; symlinked parents; separator-bearing labels. `yml.rs:337`, `clear.rs:158`, `fs_utils.rs:1`. | Reject unsafe destructive destinations before writes; resolve identity/overlap and staging aliases; protect source/raw/root state. External resource paths remain valid. Test actual preservation with root/ancestor/overlap/traversal/symlink fixtures. |
| VERSION and outputs change before hooks; rollback covers only the execution middle. `build.rs:236`, `build.rs:328`. | Stage managed writes and cover hooks, snapshots, execution, postprocessing and promotion with complete error handling. Restore exact prior managed state, including VERSION absence/bytes. |
| Public docs cleared before ignored promotion failures; post-cleanup precedes CAS export. `build.rs:359`, `build.rs:370`, `build.rs:430`. | Require successful expected-output promotion and archive real output bytes before cleanup; never report success after failed/missing promotion. Preserve the previous release on failure. |
| Environment read errors suppressed through `lines().flatten()`; invalid names can panic; required files can be ignored. `env.rs:69`, `env.rs:181`. | Bounded reads, validation before mutation, explicit errors for directory/unreadable/empty/NUL inputs; prove analysis never starts. |
| Environment guard mutates process-wide variables across library builds. `env.rs:118`. | Resolve a per-run map and apply child-command environment explicitly. Overlapping projects must not exchange variables/profiles/credentials or change caller environment. A private mutex cannot protect unrelated readers. |
| Credential helper embeds tokens in arguments/shell text, ignores requested host and inherited-helper behavior. `git.rs:146`. | Prefer native configured authentication. Any override needs fixed code, exact host scope and no secret in argv/source. Use synthetic punctuation-bearing sentinels and mocked Git; never real credentials in logs. |
| Optional Git work runs implicitly; fetch despite disabled checks, duplicate commits, hardcoded branch and discarded token. `build_pre.rs:112`, `build.rs` final Git stages. | Execute only requested operations using real upstream/native auth; handle clean commits and separate local success from publication failure. Mock Git/network tests. |

## Additional correctness findings

| Finding and baseline source | Required correction and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Literal root metacharacters become script glob syntax. `build.rs:650`, `build.rs:681`. | Escape literal root only, keep user include/exclude syntax; verify actual analysis bytes in bracket/space-named roots. |
| Renderer YAML rewritten persistently, malformed YAML replaced by empty mapping and restoration loses original text/keys. `build.rs:709`, `build.rs:338`. | Validate early; prefer supported renderer controls, otherwise exact-byte restoration on every exit. |
| Individual documents ignore configured docs destination; PDF/DOCX formats guessed as HTML; promotion errors discarded. `build.rs:271`, `build.rs:363`, `build_pre.rs:79`. | One validated destination and explicit supported format mapping; reject unsupported formats rather than guessing; require actual expected artifacts. |
| Rmd filename interpolated into executable R source. `build.rs:990`. | Pass data/arguments to fixed R code; test spaces, apostrophes, backslashes and Unicode without local R execution. |
| Remote paths stay invocation-relative and invalid content tags/errors are dropped. `yml.rs:429`, `build.rs:435`. | Normalize paths against the captured root, validate content tags before writes and propagate export failures. |
| CAS path normalization can collide on Unix; scan/copy race can store bytes under the wrong digest. `cas.rs:202`, `cas.rs:248`. | Preserve platform path distinctions or reject unsupported names; verify stored bytes against digest and fail on source mutation. |
| CAS broader integrity gaps: existing-object trust, unsafe boundaries, non-atomic manifest, CSV escaping, existence-only verification, malformed digest/path traversal and missing/file source accepted as empty snapshot. | Extend existing CAS work rather than claim a redesign is complete. Require a real input directory and fixture-backed integrity/error behavior. |
| Unsupported control keys silently filtered; runtime invents directory defaults/subpaths. `yml.rs` filtering/validation/get_path. | Enforce approved active configuration and explicit used mappings, reject unsupported behavior settings before mutations. Init alone may write defaults. |

## Scope and implementation order

After bounded configuration fixes: destructive-path guards; complete managed-state
failure/promotion handling; per-run environment; Git authentication/operation
corrections; exact path/context behavior; explicit renderer checks. Each focused
change needs actual Ponytail full-mode review, an independent review and remote
regressions. Record implemented evidence in the [compatibility log](compatibility.qmd).

Managed-state restoration cannot undo arbitrary external effects of user scripts
or hooks. This is not an OS sandbox or global rollback promise. No trustworthy
production-release safety claim follows from preview tests or this static audit.
The existing R package and thesis remain untouched.

The project already uses Rust edition 2024. Do not modernize for syntax alone.
Rust 1.85 is only an MSRV candidate until the locked dependency graph is tested.
Release builds should use reviewed stable Rust and `--locked`; add fmt, clippy and
documentation checks without duplicating every matrix unnecessarily. A future
fixture-backed YAML dependency migration is separate from urgent correctness fixes.
At current memory pressure, no local compilation, R, Docker, Quarto build or
compiling source-install is authorized; use remote tests and lightweight released
binary smoke checks.
